speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: You may cheer in the thought that you have achieved several goals but, nevertheless, berate yourself for not attaining others.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: And you probably feel frustrated and annoyed at your lack of efficacy in that regard.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Because ultimately, as human beings, we are often our own toughest critics.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: We set lofty targets for ourselves and feel like losers when we do not meet them.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: We take our own shortcomings and inflate them, diminish our best efforts and magnify our failures.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Alas, failure is very much on the minds of students in Singapore, as revealed by the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) Rankings announced in December.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: While our 15-year-old students came in second worldwide in Reading, Math and Science, we came in first for a fresh indicator.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: While we may despair that these statistics indicate our failure as a society to nurture tougher and more resilient youths, we should also take them as helpful cues for what we can do to further refine our education system, so that we can make it even more robust and forward-looking than it already is.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: This involves taking a hard look at the achievement orientation that underlies our education system, with its strong focus on examinations and grades that contribute to this fear of failure.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Achievement orientation is by no means undesirable as it propels our students to take their studies seriously, work hard and strive for excellence.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: However, an over-emphasis on achievement can also extinguish the love for learning, induce an obsession with grades and transform our students into examination-taking machines.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: I, therefore, commend the Ministry of Education (MOE) for having made concrete steps towards de-emphasising examinations at primary and secondary levels.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Instead, teachers now provide qualitative descriptors on their pupils' learning.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: While some may denigrate these as mere symbolic efforts, we cannot underestimate the power of symbolism.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Indeed, there is yet more that we can do to lessen the achievement orientation and downplay the fear of failure, both symbolically and practically, particularly at the operational level.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: First, let us cast our eye on our students’ everyday learning environments.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: I am assured that most of our teachers work hard at their jobs and do their best to instil excellence and industry in their students.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: However, a small minority engage in microaggressions in the classroom where they use questionable tactics and harsh measures to motivate underperforming students.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: As distressed students and parents have shared with me, these include reading out the names and test scores of every student in class in order of highest to lowest scorers, thereby prolonging the ordeal for those at the bottom of the pile.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Another often mentioned practice is the flashing of the work of poor performers on the screen and using these as examples of what not to do, with the identity of the "incompetent" student being made clearly known to everyone.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Teachers have also been known to taunt students with disparaging comments, such as "you’re too stupid to take this course" or "why can’t you do something so simple?" In more extreme situations, some teachers promise the entire class a fast-food treat if everyone in the class scores above a certain threshold.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: When some pupils fail to attain that magic score, the teacher then denies everyone the treat and the disappointed class then chastises and ostracises the underperformers.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Such tactics not only shame the poor performers but also create a toxic environment that promotes dog-eat-dog hostility rather than peer-to-peer support.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that these teachers are fundamentally well-intentioned and seek only to spur on their students.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: And their actions are really symptomatic of the broader pressures that teachers themselves face in delivering results.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Be that as it may, such teachers must be made to realise that these destructive methods of highlighting failure and underperformance can demotivate students and lead them to lose interest in the subject.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: They can also demoralise the students and, at worst, inflict long-term damage on their self-esteem.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: As worries about the mental health of young people are on the ascent, we must not dismiss such microaggressions in the classroom and do our utmost to educate our teachers on their harms.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: I, therefore, propose that we better prepare and empower our teachers to be proactive and sensitive in helping students manage failure and deal with setbacks.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Our schools must feel like safe spaces in which to fail and to try again.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Second, even as we have de-emphasised class rankings in report books, teachers are communicating actively with parents about their children via a range of mobile apps and digital platforms, including Parents Gateway, ClassDojo, Remind and even WhatsApp.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: In research for my book "Transcendent Parenting: Raising Children in the Digital Age", we captured screenshots from parents’ phones where teachers would message parents of their children's performance in individual tests and assignments.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Yet another teacher messaged the parents that 30 pupils had scored full marks for a spelling test.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: If our average class size is 33-34, how would the three or four kids who missed out on a perfect score feel?

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: I reckon that those kids and their parents must have felt like failures.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Furthermore, apps like ClassDojo also allow teachers to assign a score to children's in-class performance and this is also communicated to the parents, thereby allowing parents to "track" how their children are faring in class.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: My research also showed that some parents obsess over these scores and interrogate their children about what went on in school, even though these scores are disguised as gamified rewards.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Some may argue that it is parents and, indeed, students themselves who are keen to know how well they are doing.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: However, we can collectively reshape the culture of achievement orientation if there is an overall shift in emphasis from relative performance towards individual performance, and where qualitative feedback is prioritised over quantitative metrics.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Third, another setting in which our students feel the fear of failure most acutely is in the collection of the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE), GCE "O" and "A" level results.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Many students and families are on tenterhooks in the days leading up to these fateful moments.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Those who have performed beyond or up to expectations will be relieved but those who have not will find the entire exercise excruciating.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Besides the seemingly interminable wait for the results, there is also the awkward trudge out of school where friends will demand to know how well you have performed.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Some students have been known to call the walk out from the school hall to the school gate the walk of shame.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Others hide in the toilet until the coast is clear!

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Mind you, many students will feel like they have failed, even if they have done well by objective measures.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: In one junior college (JC) where students with 6As and above were invited on stage, some students with 5As cried buckets.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: In another school where the average International Baccalaureate (IB) score was 43, one student who scored an admirable 41 points was seen bawling his eyes out.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Ultimately, the atmosphere around the collection of results for these high stakes examinations is stressful and intense.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Must we pile on the pressure by requiring that students collect them personally?

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: An already difficult experience exacerbated by the prevalence of smartphones to capture and broadcast everything via social media?

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Let us not forget that our young lead very public lives where they have an online image to maintain and live up to, thereby adding to their social anxiety around such watershed events.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: I reiterate that the Programme for International Student Assessment (PISA) measure found that a sizeable majority of our students worry about what others would think of them if they fail.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: By removing the public spectacle with which these results are released, we can lessen the perception that these exams are as high stakes as currently viewed.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: We will also send the clear message that they are not the be all and end all of each student’s educational journey.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: As for students who have excelled, we can still mark their successes in other ways, such as through the Edusave Award ceremonies that showcase achievements by students across all levels.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: By turning off the glaring spotlight on the collection of results for high stakes examinations, we also send the important signal that ours is a culture of lifelong learning that does not end with attaining these certificates.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: After all, in the wake of Industry 4.0 and beyond, we must all recognise that learning extends well beyond our formal school years.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: I believe that through these measures big and small, that we can help to further reduce achievement orientation in our education system and, in the process, mitigate the fear of failure.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: As they say, there is nothing to fear but fear itself.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Failure can be instructive and rewarding, providing us with feedback and valuable experience for future undertakings.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: But it is the fear of failure that holds us back.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
text: Let us do our best to make sure that they are fearless, too.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Failure teaches us valuable lessons, and learning to bounce back from setbacks is one of the most critical lifeskills that our students can learn.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: My response will elaborate on three points: first, the value of failure and what our teachers are doing to inculcate a growth mindset in our students; second, the systems changes that MOE is making so that students can develop to their fullest potential; third, our collective effort in reshaping societal attitudes, helping students to learn from setbacks and grow in confidence.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Parents, alongside educators, also have an important role to play.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: MOE has looked into the PISA findings that Prof Lim mentioned earlier.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In MOE's studies, students report that they are stressed by high expectations from themselves and others.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At the same time, the PISA findings also indicated that our students have higher levels of self-efficacy, which reflects confidence in one's ability to get things done, compared to peers in other top-performing education systems.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Hence, the fear of failure may actually be a reflection of the strong achievement motivation and expectations of our students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Just like stress, a healthy level of concern about failure is not a bad thing.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In other words, we do not always have to fear the "fear of failure".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Nonetheless, we agree that excessive fear of failure is undesirable.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It can lead to risk-aversion, anxiety and a reluctance to try new challenges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: As everybody can attest to, experiencing failure is an unavoidable part of life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In fact, some successful entrepreneurs will tell you that it is actually an essential stepping-stone on the way to success.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Hence, we must teach our students how to get up when they fall and to manage the challenges and stressors that they may face, whether in school or in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, our schools and teachers provide opportunities for students to face challenges and openly discuss success and failure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Schools promote a supportive learning culture, whereby positive teacher-student relationship and peer support are emphasised.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our teachers are trained to use different means to motivate their charges.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They use role models and positive peer examples to encourage the class to excel.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Teachers also help students to see that there is no need to be overly anxious over "failures".

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Instead, they are just setbacks that provide useful learning points and feedback in their lifelong journey, and the "try-fail-try-again" approach can provide a richer learning experience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: There may be instances where these can be done better and we note the feedback given by Prof Lim Sun Sun.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Developing resilience in the face of failure is also proactively inculcated as part of Character and Citizenship Education (CCE) that all students experience.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through CCE, students learn about a growth mindset and understand that their abilities can be developed through dedication and a never-say-die attitude.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Beyond classroom lessons, our students reinforce these skills through co-curricular activities (CCA) interactions, inter-school competitions and even student body elections.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These experiences enable them to overcome challenges, taste success and learn from setbacks.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: At this point, let me share the thinking behind the collection of national examination results.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: First, it is important that when students receive their results, regardless of whether it meets their expectations or beyond, that they have the support of their closest friends, teachers and school counsellors at hand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: So, it is important that they are present.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Second, we have seen that this is the juncture where many students look to their teachers for timely and relevant advice regarding their next phase of education.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Some schools also give out results at the classroom level, rather than in the school hall.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We will continue to review how schools release results, in the best interests of students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Moving on to my second point, indeed, I fully agree with Prof Lim Sun Sun that we should nurture a culture of lifelong learning and thank her for her support in the changes we are making at MOE.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: New pathways, increased porosity between them, and a greater diversity of programmes cater to the diverse strengths and aspirations of our students and give them the chance to chart a different path, or to try again.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: These pathways recognise our student's achievements beyond examinations and support them to develop and pursue their strengths and interests.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: It mitigates the high stakes of examinations and reduces an overemphasis on academic results.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Instead, they can discover and develop their potential and take a combination of subjects across different levels that cater to their strengths.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: In our IHLs, students have continuous opportunities to upgrade so that they can always try again or further their education subsequently.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Working adults can return to full-time studies at the polytechnics via the Early Admissions Exercise.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Among polytechnic graduates, many go on to pursue a university degree.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: University graduates may further their education through a specialist diploma in a polytechnic.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Everyone can continue to acquire new skills or deepen their skills throughout life, through a wide range of continuing education and training opportunities that are supported by SkillsFuture Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: We are also encouraging students to go beyond their comfort zone through diverse educational programmes that provide opportunities for students to chart their own path.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: One of the students I have met over the years is Alif Adam, a Ngee Ann Polytechnic graduate who now runs an e-commerce business in fitness wear.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Alif dropped out of JC twice, before he found his footing in polytechnic where he discovered his natural talent as an entrepreneur.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Today, he still goes back to Ngee Ann Polytechnic to inspire and mentor students.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: This leads me to my third and final point – how we, as a society, can also shift our mindsets.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our education system is increasingly one where our students can customise their goals based on their own definition of success.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: They can take advantage of many "bridges" and "ladders" in their lifelong journey of learning.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Our schools and our teachers also create a supportive environment where our students feel safe to challenge themselves, rather than hold back due to a fear of failure.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: All of these will help students to be more resilient, self-reliant and innovative.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: By showing timely support and seizing teachable moments, we can provide a nurturing environment for our children to be comfortable with confronting failures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: For example, as parents, when our children do not perform as well as expected, we could emphasise that what matters more is how they pick themselves up.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Guide our children to turn their disappointment into a source of motivation to do better the next time and to never lose belief in themselves.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Through actions, big and small, we can become a society of opportunities for everybody by doing our part to provide that "trampoline" for our children to bounce back from setbacks and set their eyes on greater heights.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education and Minister for Social and Family Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim)
text: Together with parents and teachers, MOE will nurture the next generation of resilient Singaporeans who are ready for the future.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun
text: It may well be that there are some students who prefer the comforts of their teachers, but there are also very many students who would much prefer to check the results in the privacy and comfort of their home away from the public glare.

speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun
text: So, I think this is something that is worthy of being investigated.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And, at the same time, we want to make sure that there are opportunities for the kids to get guidance during that process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I have seen and I have heard, because I have my own children, even after the results are out, the kids do get together and support one another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And, to me, that part is critical because that is where you continue to build the bond, the support and go through that educational journey with your friends.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is not only about pressure or about the fear of failure.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: It is also about how we look at the educational journey as not only about my own journey – it is my journey with my friends, with my teachers and the community at large.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: That is the reason why, in my answer, I shared that while the teachers will do one thing, and we are trying to improve ourselves and continue to refine the system, it is also the bigger society, the bigger support system and the people around the kid that will actually enrich and make the whole process holistic for the child in his or her educational journey.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: As I said earlier, it is something that we will continue to refine and we thank Prof Lim Sun Sun for her suggestions and what she had shared with us today.
